plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A graceful ornamental tree that covers its branches in clouds of pale pink-white, almond-scented blossoms before the leaves emerge. It is the most widely planted cherry for hanazakura festivals and is a hallmark of early spring in temperate regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid April in Japan and the mid-Atlantic US; earlier in warmer areas of southern Japan and Korea
plants.location: Japan, South Korea, Washington D.C. (USA), and temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: The Yoshino cherry trees around the Tidal Basin in Washington D.C. were a 1912 gift from Tokyo, and in warm years they can begin blooming around mid-March.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A hardy bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers and blue-green strap-like leaves. It naturalizes in woodlands and meadows and is a classic harbinger of spring in Western Europe, with countless garden cultivars derived from it.
plants.location: Western Europe, especially the UK, France, and Belgium; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: Daffodils contain lycorine and other alkaloids that make them toxic to most animals, which is why deer and rodents usually leave them alone. One alkaloid, galantamine, is used in medicine for Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Magnolia × soulangeana
plants.description: A deciduous small tree or large shrub bearing large, tulip-shaped goblet flowers on bare branches in early spring. The blooms are white to pink-purple, often flushed darker at the base, and they can be spectacular in gardens and parks.
plants.location: Cultivated across temperate Asia, Europe, and North America (hybrid originated in France)
plants.funFact: Magnolias are among the most ancient flowering plants, and their flowers evolved before bees existed, so they are pollinated by beetles. The hybrid was first raised in France in the 1820s by Étienne Soulange-Bodin.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A fast-growing subtropical tree with fern-like leaves and dense panicles of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere, some trees still carry late-season blooms in early autumn, and the carpets of fallen petals are striking.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly October to December in the Southern Hemisphere, with a secondary or lingering bloom into March in some locations; spring (April to June) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in Australia, South Africa, and California
plants.funFact: In Sydney, Australia, jacaranda blooms are a signature of the end of the year, and in Pretoria, South Africa, the city is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of its tens of thousands of trees.
